prompt: A network diagram has 7 routers and the designer claims each router has exactly 3 direct links to other routers. What can you conclude? Treat links as undirected point-to-point edges.

options.explanation: 21 is the sum of degrees. Each link is counted at both ends, so the number of links would be 21 / 2 = 10.5, which isn't a whole number.
Correct. By the handshaking lemma the sum of degrees is twice the number of edges, so it must be even. 7 × 3 = 21 is odd.

options.text: The design has 10 or 11 links depending on the layout
options.explanation: The number of edges is exactly half the degree sum, with no flexibility. Since 21/2 isn't an integer, no layout exists.

options.text: The design is possible only if the graph is a tree
options.explanation: A tree on 7 vertices has 6 edges and degree sum 12, not 21. In any case the parity argument rules out every graph.

workedExample: Every undirected link contributes two edge ends. Seven routers each contributing an odd count give an odd total, so no whole set of undirected links can realise the design. Rearranging the drawing cannot repair a parity contradiction.
